name: settings-appearance
title: Settings: Appearance
texts: System follows your Mac. Light and Dark stay as you set them.
Straft Default. The standard Straft Studio look.
Black and White. Black text on white in Light mode, white text on black in Dark mode.
Studio Amber. Warm and neutral. An all-day workhorse.
Slate Noir. Graphite and steel. The interface steps back so the story leads.
Midnight Reel. Deep navy for late editing nights.
Teal & Orange. The blockbuster grade: cool surfaces, warm action.
Courier & Cream. A parchment writing room with brick-red ink.
Cutting Room. Restful sage green for editors.
Velvet Curtain. Theatre burgundy and gold. Premiere night.

name: settings-appearance-scrolled

Arctic Frame. Crisp daylight for schedules and budgets.

Location Scout. Earthy olive. Grounded and calm.
Desert Dune. Sand and rust, soft on the eyes.
Colorist Neutral. True grey. No colour cast around your images.

texts: Straft AI runs on this computer after a one-time download. Your project data is not sent to Straft Studio or to an AI cloud service.
Straft Studio works normally without Straft AI.
A one-time download of 1.24 GB. It needs 1.78 GB of free space (26.62 GB free on this drive).
The download uses the internet once. After it, Straft AI works on this computer without the internet, and your projects are never sent anywhere.
No requests yet. The figures appear after you use Straft AI.
Only numbers are kept on this computer: no questions, answers or project text. Nothing is sent. Export AI report saves them to a file you choose, to share if you want to.

name: settings-diagnostics
title: Settings: Diagnostics
texts: A diagnostics bundle helps the team find a problem. It never contains your project text. You choose where it is saved and whether to send it.
manifest.json, List of every file in this bundle, what it contains and its SHA-256 checksum. (2 KB)
summary.json, Straft Studio version, Windows version, architecture, distribution channel and database schema versions. (778 bytes)
errors.json, Error codes from recent logs, with how often and when they occurred. (154 bytes)
timings.json, How long slow or failed operations took, by operation name. (119 bytes)
log-tail.txt, The most recent log entries, rebuilt from fixed messages, operation names, error codes and numbers only. (299 bytes)
ai-status.json, Straft AI status: available or not, bundle check, engine state and component versions. No folders or file paths. (1 KB)

INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
A small office behind a barred window. Shelves of forgotten things: umbrellas, a single shoe, a birdcage with no bird, a box of keys labelled by year.
DEVI (60s, cardigan over a railway uniform, reading glasses) eats peanuts from a paper cone and fills in a REGISTER in slow, neat capitals.
A knock on the window bars. She looks up.
KIRAN (12, school bag, hair wet from the washroom tap) stands on tiptoe to see over the counter.
Did anyone hand in a kite?
Did anyone hand in a kite? A red one.
Red. A long tail made of newspaper. It says KIRAN on the back in marker.
Devi runs a finger down the register.
No kites. One goat, last Tuesday. He was collected.

1 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT1
A small office behind a barred window. Shelves of forgotten things: umbrellas, a single shoe, a birdcage with no bird, a box of keys labelled by year.
DEVI (60s, cardigan over a railway uniform, reading glasses) eats peanuts from a paper cone and fills in a REGISTER in slow, neat capitals.
A knock on the window bars. She looks up.
KIRAN (12, school bag, hair wet from the washroom tap) stands on tiptoe to see over the counter.
KIRAN Did anyone hand in a kite?
KIRAN Red. A long tail made of newspaper. It says KIRAN on the back in marker.
Devi runs a finger down the register.
DEVI No kites. One goat, last Tuesday. He was collected.
He is gone before she can answer.
A long platform under yellow lamps. A goods train clanks past without stopping. Kiran sits on a bench with his knees pulled up, watching the sky above the station roof.
3 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT3
The next night. The same knock. Devi does not look up.
4 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT4
The night after. Devi already has her finger on the register when the knock comes.
DEVI (before he speaks) Still no kites.
KIRAN How do you know I came for the
DEVI Nobody comes three nights in a row for a shoe.
He almost smiles. Then he goes.
Devi watches the empty window. She closes the register.
5 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - STORE ROOM - NIGHT5
A long, low room under the platforms. Cages of sacks and crates. A single TUBE LIGHT that buzzes and flickers.
Devi walks along the shelves with a TORCH. She lifts tarpaulins, opens crates, moves a broken harmonium.
Behind a stack of suitcases, something red. She pulls it
A KITE, its frame snapped in two places, the paper torn. The newspaper tail is tangled around a suitcase handle. On the back, in marker: KIRAN.
6 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT6
The kite lies on the counter. Devi sits with a pot of GLUE, a roll of TAPE and two thin BAMBOO STICKS cut from a broom.
She splints the frame. She patches the tear with a page from the register, the blank side out. Her hands know the work.
DEVI I know. Your name is on it.
DEVI It was broken. Now it is mended. Those are different.
She slides it under the bars. He holds it as if it might break again.
KIRAN My father made it. Before he went to work in the city.
DEVI Then he will want to know it still
The footbridge over the tracks. Wind rattles the iron railings. Kiran and Devi climb the steps, Devi slower, one hand on the rail.
DEVI I am not running. Do not ask me to
KIRAN You do not have to run. You only have to hold it up.
Devi holds the kite high over her head. Kiran walks backwards, paying out the string from a SPOOL.
She lets go. The kite dips toward the tracks, then catches the wind and climbs.
It rises over the station roof, the newspaper tail snapping behind it. Kiran laughs out loud.
A night train slides beneath them, every window lit. Passengers look up.
9 INT. NIGHT TRAIN - SECOND CLASS COMPARTMENT - CONTINUOUS9
A tired MAN (30s, work clothes, lunch tin on his lap) looks out of the window. He sees a red kite above the station. He sits up.
He presses his hand flat against the glass.
Grey light. The kite still flies. Kiran sits on the bridge floor with the string tied around his wrist, asleep against the railing.
Devi sits beside him, peanuts in her lap. She takes out the REGISTER and writes in her slow, neat capitals:
She closes the book and looks up at the kite.

1 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT1
A small office behind a barred window. Shelves of forgotten things: umbrellas, a single shoe, a birdcage with no bird, a box of keys labelled by year.
DEVI (60s, cardigan over a railway uniform, reading glasses) eats peanuts from a paper cone and fills in a REGISTER in slow, neat capitals.
A knock on the window bars. She looks up.
KIRAN (12, school bag, hair wet from the washroom tap) stands on tiptoe to see over the counter.
KIRAN Did anyone hand in a kite?
KIRAN Red. A long tail made of newspaper. It says KIRAN on the back in marker.
Devi runs a finger down the register.
DEVI No kites. One goat, last Tuesday. He was collected.
He is gone before she can answer.
A long platform under yellow lamps. A goods train clanks past without stopping. Kiran sits on a bench with his knees pulled up, watching the sky above the station roof.
3 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT3
The next night. The same knock. Devi does not look up.
4 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT4
The night after. Devi already has her finger on the register when the knock comes.
DEVI (before he speaks) Still no kites.
KIRAN How do you know I came for the
DEVI Nobody comes three nights in a row for a shoe.
He almost smiles. Then he goes.
Devi watches the empty window. She closes the register.
5 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - STORE ROOM - NIGHT5
A long, low room under the platforms. Cages of sacks and crates. A single TUBE LIGHT that buzzes and flickers.
Devi walks along the shelves with a TORCH. She lifts tarpaulins, opens crates, moves a broken harmonium.
Behind a stack of suitcases, something red. She pulls it
A KITE, its frame snapped in two places, the paper torn. The newspaper tail is tangled around a suitcase handle. On the back, in marker: KIRAN.
6 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT6
The kite lies on the counter. Devi sits with a pot of GLUE, a roll of TAPE and two thin BAMBOO STICKS cut from a broom.
She splints the frame. She patches the tear with a page from the register, the blank side out. Her hands know the work.
DEVI I know. Your name is on it.
DEVI It was broken. Now it is mended. Those are different.
She slides it under the bars. He holds it as if it might break again.
KIRAN My father made it. Before he went to work in the city.
DEVI Then he will want to know it still
The footbridge over the tracks. Wind rattles the iron railings. Kiran and Devi climb the steps, Devi slower, one hand on the rail.
DEVI I am not running. Do not ask me to
KIRAN You do not have to run. You only have to hold it up.
Devi holds the kite high over her head. Kiran walks backwards, paying out the string from a SPOOL.
She lets go. The kite dips toward the tracks, then catches the wind and climbs.
It rises over the station roof, the newspaper tail snapping behind it. Kiran laughs out loud.
A night train slides beneath them, every window lit. Passengers look up.
9 INT. NIGHT TRAIN - SECOND CLASS COMPARTMENT - CONTINUOUS9
A tired MAN (30s, work clothes, lunch tin on his lap) looks out of the window. He sees a red kite above the station. He sits up.
He presses his hand flat against the glass.
Grey light. The kite still flies. Kiran sits on the bridge floor with the string tied around his wrist, asleep against the railing.
Devi sits beside him, peanuts in her lap. She takes out the REGISTER and writes in her slow, neat capitals:
She closes the book and looks up at the kite.

Meera works the night shift at the city hospital. Every night she takes the last bus home. One night the bus does not come, and the driver of the next one will not wait. She walks, and on the way she finds a lost bag with a ticket for a bus that left ten years ago. By dawn at the depot she knows who it belongs to.

NIGHT BUS · SIDES · SHOOT DAY 1 · Example-Short (imported)
1. INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT
A small office behind a barred window. Shelves of forgotten things: umbrellas, a single shoe, a birdcage with no bird, a box of keys labelled by year.
DEVI (60s, cardigan over a railway uniform, reading glasses) eats peanuts from a paper cone and fills in a REGISTER in slow, neat capitals.
A knock on the window bars. She looks up.
KIRAN (12, school bag, hair wet from the washroom tap) stands on tiptoe to see over the counter.
Did anyone hand in a kite?
Red. A long tail made of newspaper. It says KIRAN on the back in marker.
Devi runs a finger down the register.
No kites. One goat, last Tuesday. He was collected.
He is gone before she can answer.
A long platform under yellow lamps. A goods train clanks past without stopping. Kiran sits on a bench with his knees pulled up, watching the sky above the station roof.

Every person and place in this script is invented. Running time is about 12 minutes.
Copyright 2026 Straft Studio. Fictional sample written for Straft Studio; you may use it to learn the app. 2026-10-07
1 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT1
A small office behind a barred window. Shelves of forgotten things: umbrellas, a single shoe, a birdcage with no bird, a box of keys labelled by year.
DEVI (60s, cardigan over a railway uniform, reading glasses) eats peanuts from a paper cone and fills in a REGISTER in slow, neat capitals.
A knock on the window bars. She looks up.
KIRAN (12, school bag, hair wet from the washroom tap) stands on tiptoe to see over the counter.
KIRAN Did anyone hand in a kite?
KIRAN Red. A long tail made of newspaper. It says KIRAN on the back in marker.
Devi runs a finger down the register.
DEVI No kites. One goat, last Tuesday. He was collected.
He is gone before she can answer.
A long platform under yellow lamps. A goods train clanks past without stopping. Kiran sits on a bench with his knees pulled up, watching the sky above the station roof.
3 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT3
The next night. The same knock. Devi does not look up.
4 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT4
The night after. Devi already has her finger on the register when the knock comes.
DEVI (before he speaks) Still no kites.
KIRAN How do you know I came for the
DEVI Nobody comes three nights in a row for a shoe.
He almost smiles. Then he goes.
Devi watches the empty window. She closes the register.
5 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - STORE ROOM - NIGHT5
A long, low room under the platforms. Cages of sacks and crates. A single TUBE LIGHT that buzzes and flickers.
Devi walks along the shelves with a TORCH. She lifts tarpaulins, opens crates, moves a broken harmonium.
Behind a stack of suitcases, something red. She pulls it
A KITE, its frame snapped in two places, the paper torn. The newspaper tail is tangled around a suitcase handle. On the back, in marker: KIRAN.
6 INT. KESARGANJ JUNCTION - LOST PROPERTY OFFICE - NIGHT6
The kite lies on the counter. Devi sits with a pot of GLUE, a roll of TAPE and two thin BAMBOO STICKS cut from a broom.
She splints the frame. She patches the tear with a page from the register, the blank side out. Her hands know the work.
DEVI I know. Your name is on it.
DEVI It was broken. Now it is mended. Those are different.
She slides it under the bars. He holds it as if it might break again.
KIRAN My father made it. Before he went to work in the city.
DEVI Then he will want to know it still
The footbridge over the tracks. Wind rattles the iron railings. Kiran and Devi climb the steps, Devi slower, one hand on the rail.
DEVI I am not running. Do not ask me to
KIRAN You do not have to run. You only have to hold it up.
Devi holds the kite high over her head. Kiran walks backwards, paying out the string from a SPOOL.
She lets go. The kite dips toward the tracks, then catches the wind and climbs.
It rises over the station roof, the newspaper tail snapping behind it. Kiran laughs out loud.
A night train slides beneath them, every window lit. Passengers look up.
9 INT. NIGHT TRAIN - SECOND CLASS COMPARTMENT - CONTINUOUS9
A tired MAN (30s, work clothes, lunch tin on his lap) looks out of the window. He sees a red kite above the station. He sits up.
He presses his hand flat against the glass.
Grey light. The kite still flies. Kiran sits on the bridge floor with the string tied around his wrist, asleep against the railing.
Devi sits beside him, peanuts in her lap. She takes out the REGISTER and writes in her slow, neat capitals:
She closes the book and looks up at the kite.
